_readme: Skyloft Austin, 507 W 23rd St, as js/slopes-apartments.js draws it. Every number cites a key from `sources` in a sibling `_src`; a value with no source says so. Metres, in the footprint's own oriented bounding box (js/westcampus.js obbOf): L=62.54, W=35.79, +u runs NORTH at bearing 4.5 deg, so u=0 is the SOUTH end and u=62.54 the 23rd Street end; +v runs WEST, so v=0 is the EAST edge and v=35.79 the Nueces edge. Read docs/apartments.md for the schema.
name: Skyloft Austin

sources.S1: data/snapshots/2026-08-27/buildings.detailed.geojson feature 4c485eb1-3a42-4633-9f67-df5e1c155b5a: name 'Skyloft Austin', num_floors 18, final_height 57.9 (source_height 'overture'), and a THREE-ring polygon - a 62.54 x 35.79 m rectangle with two interior rings of 63 m2 each. Overpass was not reachable from this machine during the pass, so no OSM way id is quoted; the outline is the snapshot's, verbatim.
sources.S2: scripts/bake_westcampus.py, TIER ONE entry 'Skyloft Austin' and its header: '2018, 18 storeys, 442,000 sq ft. The source polygon has TWO 63 m2 holes in it and they are real: the z20 nadir shows two light wells cut clean through the roof plane... Pool on the main roof at the south end (nadir).' Its values: base 6.2 m of BASE_GLASS #454b51, tower #93a3ac, crown 4.0 m of CROWN_COOL #9aa1a6, mech 3.8, deck 'roof', pool (2.0, -22.0, 5.0, 12.0).
sources.S3: Mark Hart Architecture, markhartarch.com/skyloft (the architect's own project page): 18 stories, 442,000 SF, 2018, rooftop pool, furnished apartments, market, study areas, fitness centre, parking, bike parking.
sources.S4: apartments.com / apartmentfinder.com listing for Skyloft Austin, 507 W 23rd St, Austin TX 78705: built 2018, 18 stories, 212 units, '18th-story rooftop pool'. The address is what fixes the building on 23rd St.
sources.S5: markhartarch.com/skyloft photograph 4 of 13 (Leonid Furmansky; saved as mha_04.jpg, 1000x1500): the whole tower in full sun against a blue sky - the near-white panel field with its regular punched-window grid on the long face, a distinctly darker grey panel podium of six storeys under it, a blank end wall carrying scattered narrow slot windows on the same near-white panel, and a glazed amenity volume with a canopy at the top.
sources.S6: mha_02.jpg (1000x1500): the exposed board-marked concrete lift and stair core running the whole height, a full-height glazed stair beside it with a landing at every floor, a mid blue-grey panel plane with scattered slot windows on its other side, the white mass stepping down in terraces to the left, and a dark teal-blue clad cap box with a projecting soffit standing on top of the core.
sources.S7: mha_06.jpg (1500x1000): a near head-on elevation of a long face, shot from the roof of the parking garage east of the building. Ten floors and about sixteen window columns, plus a recessed bay carrying a concrete pier and a glazed stair. THIS IS THE MODULE SOURCE: floor to floor 86 px, window 45 x 55 px, column pitch 92 px, spandrel under the window 30 px.
sources.S8: mha_12.jpg (1000x1500): the Nueces / 23rd corner at blue hour (the NUECES 2300 street sign is in frame). A glazed amenity volume of about four storeys wraps the corner above a dark glazed storefront ground floor; the grey panel podium runs along both street faces; the concrete core with its teal cap stands beyond it; the white mass steps down toward this corner.
sources.S9: mha_00.jpg (1500x1000): the north elevation with the UT Tower behind it to the east - the stepped white mass, the concrete core, the glazed stair, and the grey slot-window panel field, all in one frame.
sources.S10: research/union24th-area/imagery/aerial/skyloft-austin_nadir_z20.jpg (Esri World Imagery, z20, 931x931, 0.1289 m/px at this latitude), RECTIFIED into this (u,v) frame at 10 px/m. Registration: the capture is a few degrees off nadir, so the 57.9 m roof plane sits +10, -62 px from the ground projection of the polygon (= +1.3 m east, +8.0 m north); with that shift applied the two snapshot holes land exactly on the two black light wells, which is the check. Every roof plan number below was read off that rectified plan. Features BELOW the main roof are displaced by (1 - h/57.9) x 8.0 m south in it.
sources.S11: Google Earth 3D, captured 2026-09-05 with scripts/verify/chrome.mjs on hardware GL and page.screenshot (imagery 12/3/2023). The useful frame is the one whose own readout says 30 deg 17'12.36"N 97 deg 44'36.66"W, camera 352 m, heading 180, tilt 50 - the building from the north, where the terraced north wing and its recessed terrace bands are directly visible.
sources.S12: data/roads.geojson: Nueces Street and West 23rd Street share the node (-97.74379, 30.28661), 15 m west-north-west of the building's north-west corner. So 23rd St runs along the NORTH edge and Nueces along the WEST edge, and the address 507 W 23rd St (S4) is the north-west corner.
sources.S13: js/westcampus.js SOLID: the West Campus day/golden/night trios for pool, deck paving, turf, mechanical screen and black steel rail.
sources.S14: data/hero_designs.json 'Skyloft' ('Blue glass curtain-wall tower; cool glow at night', confidence 'known'). Recorded because it is WRONG - S5 to S9 show a panel tower with punched windows and no curtain wall above the base - and because no tone here was taken from it.
sources.derived: a number computed from the sources above and marked so; 'unknown' stays unknown.

footprint._src: S1's OUTER ring verbatim. In (u,v) it is (62.54,0) (62.51,35.78) (0,35.79) (0.03,0) - a rectangle, every edge axis-parallel in the frame.
footprint._holes_src: S1's two interior rings verbatim - the two light wells, 63 m2 each. In (u,v): well A u 17.15-27.69 v 14.59-20.68, well B u 39.05-49.58 v 14.60-20.70. `footprint.holes` is NOT read by js/slopes-apartments.js; it is here because it is the measurement, and the blocks below are cut around it. See `todo`.

_frame_src: obbOf(ring) as js/westcampus.js computes it: L=62.54, W=35.79, +u bearing 4.5 deg, confirmed against the console line the generator prints at boot. S12 says which street is on which side.

levels._src: 18 storeys (S2, S3, S4) to 57.90 m (S1). The ground floor is 5.60 m - in S8 it is about 1.85x a residential floor, and S2's own base band for this building is 6.20 m; 5.60 is between them and is what makes the other 17 come out at a residential 3.015 m. Roof slab 56.85 + a 1.05 m parapet = 57.90. The per-floor split is derived; only the total and the count are sourced.
levels._height_src: 57.90 m is S1's final_height, which is Overture's - normally a guess. It is KEPT here, unlike The Standard's, because two independent sources state 18 storeys (S3, S4) and 57.90/18 = 3.22 m per storey, which is a residential floor-to-floor with a tall ground floor in it. No stated height in feet was found: SkyscraperPage and Emporis have no page for this building.

colours._src: day hex; golden and night come from js/westcampus.js's ramp() unless a full trio is given.

panel._src: the near-white fibre-cement panel field. The SAME panel in S5 reads #faf6eb in full sun (crop 445,420-505,860, the slot end wall) and #ada9a1 on the shaded long face (crop 560,600-600,625). LOOK-FIX 2: it was entered at #e3e0d8, which carries S5's warm cast (R-B = +11) into a building that is not cream, and from every camera the tower came out beige beside its grey neighbours. The hue is settled off S11 instead, where the panel can be compared with a surface of known colour in the same light: in n2_zoom the sunlit panel is #9aaaba and #9cadbd (R-B = -32, -33) and the white TPO roof membrane four metres away is #99a7b5 (R-B = -28) while the asphalt is neutral (-1) - so Earth's whole frame carries a -30 blue cast and the panel and the white membrane are the SAME hue under it. S2's own earlier read of this tower (#93a3ac) is cool for the same reason. So the day tone keeps S5's value and drops S5's light: neutral, a hair cool, at the luminance the sunlit and shaded reads bracket.

panelGrey._src: the accent panel that carries the scattered slot windows. Measured in three lights and neutralised: S6 crop 760,300-960,1300 gives #978379 under a golden evening sun, S7 crop 520,60-690,820 gives #6394c4 under a blue sky, S9 shows it a clear step darker than `panel` and greener. Each read carries its own light; the day tone is the achromatic middle.

podium._src: the darker grey panel of the six-storey base. S5 clean crops 700,875-770,905 (#9f9e9e) and 840,900-900,935 (#bbb7ad) are sunlit reads of it; S8 has it at #738dae under blue hour. LOOK-FIX 1: it was entered at #8d9295, below BOTH sunlit reads, and the six-storey base came out the darkest thing on the building from the north - darker than it is in S5, where the podium is plainly a mid grey against the white above it. Moved on to the measurement.

concrete._src: the exposed board-marked core. S6 crop 540,300-660,1300 is #c1916b in golden light, S7 crop 700,60-770,820 is #adc0d1 under a blue sky; the day tone is the neutral between them.

capBlue._src: the teal-blue cladding on the cap box over the core. S6 crop 430,270-545,330 clusters at #22749d for the lit face with #222b36 for its soffit.

mullion._src: the dark anodised curtain-wall frame of the corner amenity volume (S8): the mullions and the floor-line bands read black against the glass. S8 is blue hour, so the read is taken RELATIVE to a surface measured in daylight in the same frame - the podium panel, #a2a6a8 by day and #7ca0b6 in S8 crop 720,880-780,940, a per-channel ratio of 1.31 / 1.04 / 0.92. The mullion band (crop 470,855-600,868, 10th percentile #1e2e46) carried through that ratio is #273040; entered a step lighter and less blue because a 0.1 m frame at this camera is one pixel wide and reads as its own edge, not as its darkest core.

coping._src: parapet coping: mill-finish aluminium, the same value js/westcampus.js gives The Standard's (STD_CAP). Not separately sampled.

frame._src: window reveal strips and storefront mullions: as `coping`. Not separately sampled.

colours._glass_src: the punched windows' glass: near-black blue-grey by day. S5 crop 560,560-760,860 has the panes at #16415d at the 10th luminance percentile and S7 at #18548f - both under a blue sky, so the day value is entered without that cast; the night value is the unlit pane, and lit panes take APARTMENTS.nightLitTone.
colours._storeGlass_src: the ground-floor storefront: S8 crop 250,1180-700,1260 at blue hour is #383129 to #564e46 with the interior lit warm behind it, which is the night value. LOOK-FIX 1: the day value was that blue-hour read (#3f4c55) and the glazed corner volume came out a black rectangle at midday; a shopfront glass in daylight carries the sky, so it is lifted to #55646d.
colours._loungeGlass_src: the glass of the corner amenity volume. DERIVED, not inverted from a measurement: S8 is the only photograph of it and it is blue hour, and a large reflective plane at blue hour shows the sky, not the surface (S8 crop 470,880-540,925 is #657fab, the sky), so the daylight value cannot be read off it the way the panel's can. It is placed between the two glasses on this building that WERE derived - the punched window (#2a3a45) and the ground-floor storefront (#55646d) - because it is a full-height room glass seen against a lit interior. The night value is the warm downlit lounge S8 shows through it. LOOK-FIX 5: it was entered BELOW the storefront, at #4a5b68, and at the corner the four-storey volume read as one black block over a lighter shopfront - the same defect LOOK-FIX 1 fixed on the storefront itself, in the opposite direction. A room glass four storeys up carries more sky than a shopfront recessed under a soffit, so it is lifted a step ABOVE the storefront.
colours._stairGlass_src: the glazed stair beside the core: paler than a flat window because you see through it to a lit landing at every floor (S6, S9); cool and lit at night. LOOK-FIX 1: at #4a5f6d it read as a dark seam next to the concrete rather than the bright reflective slot S6 and S7 both show, so it is lifted two steps and now sits between the wall and the punched windows.
colours._roof_src: white membrane roof, as it reads in S10; entered cool the way S13 enters top faces.
colours._mech_src: S13 mech (mechanical penthouse screen and condenser units).
colours._terrace_src: the paving on the four terrace decks of the north wing. In S10's rectified plan the three terrace bands are the DARKEST thing on the roof plane - darker than the white membrane roofs either side of them - and S11 shows them as recessed shadowed strips behind a guard. LOOK-FIX 1: they were drawn in `roof`, the white membrane, and from the north the four steps read as bright white shelves flying out of the wall instead of as terraces.

skins._src: one rule per face treatment; every column count comes from a module in metres, never a count.

field._src: the residential long elevations. S7 head-on: floor to floor 86 px, so 0.03506 m/px at the derived 3.015 m floor; window 45 x 55 px = 1.58 x 1.93 m, column pitch 92 px = 3.23 m, spandrel under the sill 30 px = 1.05 m. Rounded to a 3.26 m bay, a 1.60 x 1.95 m window and a 0.85 m sill so the head clears the slab.

fieldGrey._src: the same window module on the grey podium: S5 shows the podium's windows in line with the tower's, one per bay per floor.

slots._src: the blank end wall in S5: near-white panel carrying narrow slot windows at about one per 6.5 m of wall per floor. In the photographs the slots are SCATTERED, not aligned; a regular 6.6 m module at the same density is what this generator can express (see `todo`). Slot 0.55 x 1.70 m is read off S5 against the 1.60 m windows two bays away.

slotsGrey._src: the same slot field on the accent panel, which is what S6, S7 and S9 show beside the core.

slotsB._src: the second slot module. The end wall is split into three strips wearing `slotsB`, `slots` and `slotsC`, whose bays (5.2 / 6.6 / 7.4 m) and sills (2.05 / 1.05 / 1.55 m) do not divide into each other, so the slots do not line up into columns - which is how they read in S5.

court._src: the four walls of each light well. No photograph shows down a well (S10's nadir reads them as black), so they wear the plainest rule the building has: the same bay, a slightly narrower window, no accent.

storefront._src: the dark glazed ground floor and the glazed corner volume above it (S8): mullions at about 1.6 m with a transom near three quarters height and a grey fascia under the floor above.

skyLounge._src: the sky lounge in the top of the tower (S5): a band of mullioned glass about two storeys tall, set BACK behind the panel plane with a soffit over it, immediately beside the open roof terrace. Panes read wider than the corner volume's - about 1.5 m against a 1.95 m window two bays away - and the reveal is 0.45 m because in S5 the glass is plainly in shadow under the plane it sits behind. The soffit itself is not drawn (see `open`).

lounge._src: ONE STOREY of the corner amenity volume (S8). Counted at the near corner of S8, where a storey is 240 px: the volume is three panes wide on each face, so the mullion pitch is 1.10 m, and there is a dark band at every floor line with the transom about seven tenths of the way up the glass. It is a per-storey rule because the volume is FOUR of them stacked; see the block's own note.

stair._src: the full-height glazed stair beside the core (S6, S7, S9): one tall pane per storey with the landing showing as a line across it.

concrete._src: the exposed core wall (S6, S8, S9): a blank concrete plane, no openings.

garage._src: the base on the two faces that are not a street - the parking podium (S3 lists parking). S5 shows it behind hoarding and S7 shows only its dark band, so the louvre pitch 0.55 m is a plausible number and is NOT measured: unknown.

_balcony_src: no balconies. S5, S6, S7, S8 and S9 show punched windows on a flat panel plane on every face, with no slab projecting anywhere; the outdoor space on this building is the terraces on the north steps and the roof.
_signs_src: no sign is modelled: no photograph in S5-S9 and no capture in S11 shows lettering on any face.

blocks._src: the 18-storey block, u 0 to 49.58, cut into six rectangles because the two light wells are HOLES in the plan and this generator's roof cap takes one ring (see `todo`). The six together are the snapshot rectangle south of u=49.58 minus the two interior rings (S1). towerS is the part south of well A.

faces._src: v0 east and u0 south face the alley and the neighbouring lot, so their base is the parking podium (S5 shows hoarding, not shopfronts, on them). v1 west is Nueces: storefront base (S8). u1 is the SOUTH wall of light well A - it is drawn across the whole width, and everything outside the well stands inside towerSE / towerSW and is never seen.

overrides._src: the south end wall is a slot field, not a window grid (S5). It is split into three strips whose bay modules do not divide into each other so the slots do not line up - see the `slots` skins. LOOK-FIX 3: the top TWO storeys of this strip are the sky lounge. S5 shows a two-storey band of mullioned glass in the top of the tower with the open roof terrace immediately beyond it, and S10's rectified plan puts the pool deck at u 0.9-8.5, v 0.9-12.0 - the south-east corner of the roof, which is the corner this strip stands under. It is the one placement the photograph and the nadir agree on; which of the two long faces S5 was shot from is in `open`. Two bands, one storey each, because the generator's storefront rule puts one transom in a band.
middle strip of the south end wall
west strip of the south end wall

The bulkhead is the mechanical penthouse; only the lift shaft inside it comes down the wall. faces._src: u0 stands against towerM. u1 is the tower's own north wall standing over the top terrace, from the 15-storey step's roof at 47.81 m up. LOOK-FIX 4: the wall that stands above the terrace to the north of it. Every north-facing face of the stepped wing was `null` with the note 'u1 is under the step to the north and is not drawn' - true only up to the NEXT step's roof; above that it is 9 m of open elevation. Four of them were missing (three steps and the tower over the top terrace), about 30 m wide each, and through the holes the camera was reading the block wall at u=39.05 on the far side of the building: in the north frame the window grids of two different steps line up exactly and are the same size, which they cannot be at two depths - one wall seen through two gaps. The riser is the residential field, from the neighbour's roof to this block's own. v1 is the EAST wall of light well B.

the teal cap box on the core (S6, S8, S9): it stands about two storeys proud of the roof in S6, so 6.2 m; it sits inside the bulkhead's plan, which is how S6 shows it - a blue box rising out of the concrete head. Its plan is derived from the bulkhead, not measured separately.

blocks._src: the north wing steps down to 23rd St in four terraces. S11 (from the north) shows the terraces directly - a recessed band with a guard at every step; S10's rectified plan shows the same three bands as long dark strips across the roof at apparent u 49.3, 54.5 and 59.0, which is where the step depths of about 3.2 m come from. The STOREY COUNTS - 15, 12, 9 and 6 - are counted off S11's mesh and are +/- 1 storey each; no drawing or elevation of this wing was found. This is the 15-storey step, u 49.58 to 52.90.

blocks._parapetTone_src: LOOK-FIX 3: the guard at the edge of a terrace, not a coping. It was `coping` - the pale mill-finish aluminium the main roof's parapet wears - and from the north the four steps read as four bright ledges laid across a grey wall, which is the reverse of the reference: in S11's own frame (earth n2) the terrace line at every step is the DARKEST thing on the north elevation, and S6 and S8 both show a dark metal guard, not a parapet, standing at each step. Same 1.05 m height, `rail` tone.

The STOREY COUNTS - 15, 12, 9 and 6 - are counted off S11's mesh and are +/- 1 storey each; no drawing or elevation of this wing was found. This is the 9-storey step, u 56.20 to 59.40.

faces._src: u0 stands against the step to the south; u1 is the riser above the next terrace north, from 20.68 m up. LOOK-FIX 4: the wall that stands above the terrace to the north of it. Every north-facing face of the stepped wing was `null` with the note 'u1 is under the step to the north and is not drawn' - true only up to the NEXT step's roof; above that it is 9 m of open elevation. Four of them were missing (three steps and the tower over the top terrace), about 30 m wide each, and through the holes the camera was reading the block wall at u=39.05 on the far side of the building: in the north frame the window grids of two different steps line up exactly and are the same size, which they cannot be at two depths - one wall seen through two gaps. The riser is the residential field, from the neighbour's roof to this block's own.

It was `coping` - the pale mill-finish aluminium the main roof's parapet wears - and from the north the four steps read as four bright ledges laid across a grey wall, which is the reverse of the reference: in S11's own frame (earth n2) the terrace line at every step is the DARKEST thing on the north elevation, and S6 and S8 both show a dark metal guard, not a parapet, standing at each step. Same 1.05 m height, `rail` tone.

overrides._src: the glazed amenity volume on the corner of 23rd and Nueces. LOOK-FIX 2, three things. (1) It was ONE storefront band from the pavement to 17.66 m, which this generator draws as a single 17.7 m pane with one transom in it - a shopfront the height of a six-storey building. S8 shows four stacked storeys of glass with a dark band at every floor line, so it is four bands of the `lounge` skin, one per storey, over the recessed storefront ground floor. (2) It was 11.3 m long on the 23rd Street face. It is about 3 panes on each face in S8, and in S11's own frame (earth n2, the base of the north elevation resampled: the 35.79 m face spans 715 px, so 20 px/m) the dark glazed corner is 90 px = 4.5 m wide - so 4.20 m, +/- 1 m. (3) On the Nueces face it was carried across two step blocks for 6.3 m; it is now the 6-storey step's own width, 3.14 m, which is inside the same tolerance and leaves no seam mid-volume. On the Nueces face the volume is this step's own width, u 59.40 to 62.54 = 3.14 m.

todo.what: polygon plans with holes, and a roof cap that earcuts them
todo.why: this building's footprint has two real interior rings (S1, S2). js/slopes-apartments.js takes ONE ring per block and caps it with B.polygon(cap), so a well cannot be a hole; the 18-storey mass is cut into six rectangles round the two wells instead. That draws the right picture - the wells are open to the sky and their four walls are drawn - but it costs six blocks where one would do, and it puts two interior walls (towerS.u1 and towerM.u0/u1) across the plan where nothing sees them. A `plan: {ring, holes}` with the holes passed to the earcut would collapse this to two blocks.

todo.what: a skin whose windows are scattered rather than on a column
todo.why: the end walls in S5, S6 and S9 carry slot windows that are deliberately NOT aligned. `bays` puts one window per bay per floor, on a column. The three strips of `slots`/`slotsB`/`slotsC` with coprime bays and different sills break the columns up, but a `scatter` rule (density per m2, position from the cell hash the pixel skin already has) would be the real thing.

todo.what: a bay whose window is a GROUP, and a chamfered corner
todo.why: two rules this building wants and the schema cannot say. (1) S7's head-on elevation repeats a wide window plus a pair of narrow ones about every 6.5 m; `bays` takes one window per bay, so the grid here is the right pitch with the wrong grouping. A `window` that took a LIST of [offset, w] inside the bay would draw it. (2) The corner amenity volume is chamfered in S8; overrides clip axis-parallel walls, so the facet cannot be drawn.

open: The four step heights (15, 12, 9 and 6 storeys) are counted off Google Earth's mesh from the north (S11) and are +/- 1 storey each. A north elevation drawing would settle them.
The east face's concrete pier and glazed stair are in S7 but S7 cannot be registered along the wall; they are placed under the roof box S10 puts at u 30-36. Position along u: +/- 5 m.
The light wells' walls were never photographed and wear the plainest skin the building has.
The roof bulkheads' heights (3.0 m, 2.2 m, 6.2 m) are derived from what stands proud in S6; only their plans are measured.
The garage louvre pitch is a plausible 0.55 m, not measured.

WHICH long face S5 was shot from is not settled. It shows one long elevation with the punched grid, a blank slot end wall beside it, a six-storey grey block in front and an open parking deck at the far edge; that reading works from the south-east and from the south-west, and the two put the sky lounge on different faces. It is placed on the strip of the SOUTH end wall that stands under the pool deck, because S10's nadir fixes the deck at the roof's south-east corner and S5 shows the lounge immediately beside the terrace. A photograph of the east elevation from the north would settle it.
The sky lounge's projecting soffit - the canopy over the glass in S5 - is not drawn. The generator has no rule for a slab that oversails a wall, and a roofItem sits on a roof, not at a band's head.

The corner amenity volume is square in plan here. In S8 its corner is CHAMFERED and each storey steps a little proud of the one above; the generator's overrides clip axis-parallel walls, so a 45-degree facet cannot be expressed.

S11's north elevation shows a dark glazed corner at the NORTH-EAST corner too, about 5 m wide, as well as the north-west one S8 photographs. It is not authored: that side of the Esri frame is in shadow and dark glass and shadow read alike there. A photograph of the alley corner would settle it.

The window rhythm is a uniform 3.26 m bay. S7's head-on elevation shows the real unit is a WIDE window with a pair of narrower ones beside it, repeating about every 6.5 m. The `bays` skin puts one window per bay per floor and cannot express a pair; the pitch and the wall-to-glass share are right, the grouping is not (see `todo`).

The north elevation has a vertical notch in it - a recess splitting the face into two wings, in S8 and in S11's own frame. The footprint here is the snapshot's rectangle with its two interior rings, which has no notch in it.
